title: Tag Invalidation
definition: The automated system RTK Query uses to know exactly WHEN to delete stale cache data and refetch it from the server. Queries 'provide' tags, and Mutations 'invalidate' tags.
simpleExplanation: You fetch a list of Posts. RTK Query labels that data with a sticky note: `['Post']`. Then, you submit a Mutation to DELETE a post. You tell the Mutation: 'When you succeed, tear up the `['Post']` sticky note'. RTK Query sees the note torn up, realizes its cache is outdated, and automatically fetches the fresh list of Posts in the background.
realWorldExample: Without Tag Invalidation, if you delete an item from a list, the item will disappear from the server, but your screen will still show it because it's stuck in the cache. Tags fix this automatically.
useCases: Keeping the UI perfectly synced with the database

intermediate: What happens immediately after a Mutation invalidates a Tag?

answers.question: Which provides?
answers.answer: Queries `providesTags` (They label the data they fetched). Mutations `invalidatesTags` (They destroy the label when they change data).

answers.question: What happens?
answers.answer: Any active Queries on the screen that provided that specific Tag will immediately and automatically trigger a background refetch to get the fresh data from the server.
